evals.prompt: Navigate Chrome to http://localhost:9876 and tell me what sections are visible on the page.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs preflight, navigates using goto, waits for a real element with wait_for_selector, then reads structure with page_context. Reports page title, headings, and nav items without taking an unnecessary screenshot.
assertions: Agent ran preflight before any browser action
Agent used wait_for_selector after goto, not a fixed wait
Agent used page_context for structural verification, not snapshot as first action
Agent did not use CDP, WSL Chrome, or headless fallback
Agent reported visible sections from page_context output

evals.prompt: Click the Metrics section in the dashboard and confirm it loaded.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses click_text to click with a visible cursor, waits for a real element with wait_for_selector, then confirms with page_context. Does not use evaluate to click, does not rely on a fixed wait, does not use screenshot as sole verification.
assertions: Agent used click_text or click_selector (visible cursor), not evaluate
Agent used wait_for_selector after the click, not a fixed wait
Agent used page_context to verify the section loaded
Agent did not use screenshot as the only verification step

evals.prompt: Fill in the search field on the current page with 'test query' and submit it.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses snapshot to find the field's selector, then fill_selector to type into it, then page_context to confirm the value is present before submitting. Does not use evaluate to fill or submit.
assertions: Agent used fill_selector, not evaluate, to type into the field
Agent verified the fill with page_context before submitting
Agent did not use evaluate to submit the form
Agent used click_text or cursor_key for submission, not evaluate

evals.prompt: Take a screenshot of the current state of the dashboard as visual proof.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs page_context first to orient, then takes a single screenshot. Reports the screenshot_path. Does not take multiple screenshots or use snapshot before page_context.
assertions: Agent ran page_context before screenshot
Agent took exactly one screenshot
Agent reported screenshot_path from the result
Agent did not use snapshot as first action

evals.prompt: I only need to see the top navigation bar — take a focused screenshot of just that area instead of the full page.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses zoom with coordinates covering the nav bar region (e.g. x0=0 y0=0 x1=1200 y1=60) instead of a full screenshot. Reports the inline base64 result. Explains that zoom is more token-efficient than a full screenshot for region-specific proof.
assertions: Agent used zoom, not screenshot, for the region-specific request
Agent supplied x0, y0, x1, y1 coordinates that target the nav area
Agent explained or acknowledged that zoom is more token-efficient than full screenshot

evals.prompt: Navigate to the login page, fill in the credentials, click Sign In, and wait for the dashboard to load.
evals.expected_output: Agent batches goto + fill_selector + click_text + wait_for_url_change (or wait_for_selector on a post-login element) in one bridge call. Does not use a fixed wait after the click. Uses wait_for_url_change to detect the redirect from the login URL.
assertions: Agent used wait_for_url_change or wait_for_selector after clicking Sign In, not a fixed wait
Agent batched all actions in one bridge call
Agent did not use evaluate to fill or submit the form
Agent verified post-login state with page_context

evals.prompt: I want to test two separate tasks in the dashboard at the same time — keep their tabs organised.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses session_name on each bridge call to route tabs into named Chrome tab groups. Uses a different session_name for each task so their tabs are visually separated in Chrome's tab strip. Explains the tab group isolation behaviour.
assertions: Agent used session_name parameter on bridge calls
Agent used distinct session_name values for the two tasks
Agent explained that tabs are grouped by session_name in Chrome

evals.prompt: The bridge isn't responding — I'm getting a socket error on every bridge call. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs preflight.sh first (self-healing). If preflight exits 0 but actions still fail, checks content_script.blocked and active tab URL. Does not attempt CDP fallback, WSL Chrome, or any alternative path.
assertions: Agent ran preflight.sh as the first recovery step
Agent did not attempt CDP, WSL Chrome, or any non-socket path
Agent checked content_script.blocked if preflight exited 0 but actions still failed
Agent used sync.sh if files were stale

evals.prompt: Preflight says the bridge is healthy but when I try to click anything it fails silently. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies this as the 'preflight exits 0 but unstable' pattern. Checks whether the active tab is chrome:// or about:newtab. If blocked, uses useSelectedTab:False with goto to open a fresh https:// tab. Does not re-run preflight in a loop.
assertions: Agent identified the blocked active tab as the likely cause
Agent checked or mentioned content_script.blocked
Agent used useSelectedTab:False to open a new tab when active tab is chrome://
Agent did not re-run preflight in a loop

evals.prompt: You've finished testing the dashboard. Perform a proper closeout.
evals.expected_output: Agent takes a screenshot (reports screenshot_path), calls page_context for final URL and title, calls bridge status to verify health, closes any tabs it opened, and ends with a handoff line stating the URL, bridge state, and tabs closed.
assertions: Agent took a screenshot and reported screenshot_path
Agent called bridge status and confirmed success:true
Agent closed any tabs it opened during the session
Agent stated a handoff line with final URL, bridge state, and tab count
Agent did not skip closeout steps despite the task being 'finished'

evals.prompt: Navigate to http://localhost:9876 and wait for the main content to appear before doing anything.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses goto followed immediately by wait_for_selector targeting a real element (h1, nav, or a known component selector) with a reasonable timeout. Does not use a fixed wait. Proceeds to page_context only after the selector resolves.
assertions: Agent used wait_for_selector after goto, not a fixed wait
Agent specified a meaningful selector (not a generic div)
Agent proceeded to page_context only after wait_for_selector resolved
Agent set a timeout on wait_for_selector

assertions: Agent identified cursor-agent.js or images/ as the surface to fix
Agent ran diagnostics to check asset presence
Agent ran sync.sh if assets needed updating
